requirements.agency: Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco (ABT)
requirements.applies_when: A Florida restaurant (or bar) wants to sell beer, wine, AND distilled spirits (full liquor) by the drink for on-premises consumption, without meeting the Special Food Service (SFS) restaurant criteria.
requirements.fees: $624-$1,820/year by county population per Fla. Stat. s. 565.02(1)(b)-(f): county population over 100,000 = $1,820; 75,001-100,000 = $1,560; 50,001-75,000 = $1,300; 25,001-50,000 = $858; 25,000 or less = $624. Temporary license = 1/4 of permanent fee or $100, whichever is greater (ABT checklist).

forms.name: DBPR ABT-6001 - Application for New Alcoholic Beverage License (with detailed instructions)

requirements.notes: ABT checklist states the 4COP category covers 'Beer, Wine and Liquor Consumption on Premises' (on-premises consumption only, not package sales). Apply online via the myfloridalicense.com Online Services link or mail/hand-deliver to an ABT district office. Applicants must complete form ABT-6001; may be required to submit fingerprints (ABT ORI# FL920150Z via FDLE Livescan vendor list; out-of-state applicants request a fingerprint card from the division), certified arrest dispositions, moral-character mitigation, right of occupancy, premises sketch, zoning approval, health approval, FEIN/SSN, contracts, partner/officer/stockholder info, Secretary of State certificate of status, and Department of Revenue clearance. Note: new 4COP quota licenses can only be issued if the county has quota availability (see FL_DRAFT_ABT_0003); most buyers acquire an existing license by transfer (see FL_DRAFT_ABT_0004).
requirements.title: 4COP quota license - beer, wine, and liquor for consumption on premises

requirements.agency: Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco (ABT)
requirements.applies_when: A bona fide food service establishment wants a full-liquor on-premises license outside the county quota by meeting food-service criteria instead of buying a quota license.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 561.20(2)(a)4 (as amended by 2023 HB 639)

forms.name: DBPR ABT-6001 - Application for New Alcoholic Beverage License (with detailed instructions)

requirements.notes: Eligibility under s. 561.20(2)(a)4 as amended in 2023 (HB 639, effective 2023): a bona fide food service establishment with at least 2,000 sq ft of service area, equipped to serve meals to 120 persons at one time, at least 120 physical seats for patrons during operating hours, holding itself out as a restaurant, deriving at least 51% of gross food and beverage revenue from food and nonalcoholic beverages. (Prior to 2023 the thresholds were 2,500 sq ft / 150 persons; the 2020 statute text confirmed on flsenate.gov.) License may NOT operate as a package store and no liquor sales after food service/consumption hours have elapsed. The 51% test is measured over the first 60-day operating period and each 12-month period thereafter; failure = revocation or denial, and the disqualified person is ineligible for a subsequent SFS application for 120 days. SFS licenses are NOT movable to a new location - valid only on the premises where issued. ABT requires Division of Hotels and Restaurants approval for SFS applications. Annual fee: ABT's 2017 fact sheet (hosted third-party but sourced to ABT) listed $1,820; current fee chart PDF did not render during research - confirm on the ABT fee chart. ABT also publishes a General Laws of Local Application and Special Acts reference (GENLAWS.pdf) because local special acts in some counties set different SFS thresholds.
requirements.title: SFS special restaurant license (non-quota full liquor, formerly 'SRX')

requirements.agency: Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco (ABT)
requirements.applies_when: Assessing whether a new 4COP quota license can be issued in a given county, or whether a quota license must be purchased from an existing holder.
requirements.notes: Statutory cap: no licenses under s. 565.02(1)(a)-(f) may be issued so that the number in any county exceeds ONE license per 7,500 residents, based on the latest regular county population estimate prepared under s. 186.901 (Bureau of Economic and Business Research, University of Florida). A new license is issued for each population increase of 7,500 residents above the April 1, 1999 baseline. Regardless of the cap, at least THREE licenses must be available in any county that approves liquor sales. Quota licenses are issued by the division subject to this limitation; when new quota capacity opens, ABT issues licenses via a drawing process (s. 561.19) - details not verified on an official source during this research. ABT publishes NO secondary-market price data; private sale prices are negotiated between parties and ABT does not set them.
requirements.title: Quota-license mechanics - county population caps and issuance

requirements.agency: Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco (ABT)
requirements.applies_when: Buying an existing 4COP quota license (or other retail license) from its current holder - the standard path to full liquor in counties with no quota availability.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 561.20; ABT transfer checklist
requirements.fees: Pay up to $5,000 for the permanent license; transfer penalty fees may apply (ABT checklist). Private purchase price negotiated between buyer and seller - ABT does not publish or regulate it.

forms.name: DBPR ABT-6002 - Application for Transfer of Ownership of an Alcoholic Beverage License

requirements.notes: ABT-6001 is for NEW licenses only - ABT instructs 'Do not use this form for a transfer of ownership of an existing license.' Transfers require division approval; the transferor must clear Department of Revenue liability (ABT-6002 includes a DOR disclosure/notarized release so the buyer can learn of potential tax liability). The division retains authority over the transfer. Special (non-quota) licenses under 561.20 may transfer only to a bona fide purchaser of the hotel/motel/restaurant facility itself (per 2023 HB 639 bill text on flsenate.gov) - an SFS license cannot be moved to a new location or sold as a standalone asset. ABT publishes no data on quota-license secondary-market prices.
requirements.title: Transfer of ownership of an alcoholic beverage license (quota license resale)

requirements.agency: Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco (ABT)
requirements.applies_when: Holding any ABT retail license (4COP, SFS, 2COP) past its first year - licenses must be renewed annually.
requirements.fees: Annual license tax (per license type/county population); delinquency penalty = $5 for each month or fraction of a month of delinquency, OR 5% of the license fee, whichever is greater.
requirements.notes: Renewal is 'as a matter of course' year to year per a division-established renewal schedule, on payment of the annual license tax and any required bond (s. 561.27(1)). A license not renewed within 60 days of expiration is CANCELED by the division unless involved in litigation/administrative action (good-cause exception at division discretion) (s. 561.27(2)). Mid-cycle applicants: full annual fee if issued more than 6 months before the next renewal date; half fee if less than 6 months.
requirements.title: Annual renewal of alcoholic beverage licenses

requirements.agency: Division of Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco (ABT)
requirements.applies_when: An alcoholic beverage license has been put into null-and-void status and the former holder wants to restore it.
requirements.fees: Fees vary depending on the length of the delinquency and the license type (ABT checklist).
requirements.notes: Submit form ABT-6015 to an ABT district office by mail, hand delivery, or by appointment. This is the official recovery path after cancellation under s. 561.27(2).
requirements.title: Delinquent renewal of a null-and-void alcoholic beverage license
